To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 5/4 binge drink measure is useful for identifying those students who are experiencing alcohol-related harms and that the 5 drink threshold measure is not a good predictor of alcohol-related harms.

the use of a higher threshold of binge drinking (e.g., > 5 drinks in a row for men or > 4 drinks in a row) in survey research does not meaningfully improve the ability to detect college students who have experienced alcohol-related harms or who have a DSM-IV diagnosis of alcohol abuse or dependence.

(a) 5/4 is a valid and reliable measure of binge drinking; (b) it is more sensitive than the NIAAA definition of binge drinking; and (c) it can be used to identify those at greatest risk for experiencing negative alcohol-related consequences.

the relationship between level of consumption (drinks) and harms.
the development of valid, useful measures of alcohol consumption that can be used to assess and prevent harms associated with alcohol consumption.
identifying the best method for measuring alcohol consumption among college students.

the 5/4 threshold measure for binge drinking provides a useful means to identify students who are at risk for negative alcohol-related consequences and who may require additional clinical assessment for prevention and intervention.

a threshold for binge drinking is a useful and valid measure for the purpose of identifying college students with alcohol-related problems and for monitoring trends in the prevalence of these problems.
the use of a summary measure of heavy drinking is an appropriate and useful tool for assessing alcohol use in college students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a single cut-point measure for binge drinking, such as the 5/4, can be used as a screening tool in college student populations to identify those at risk for experiencing alcohol-related harms.
the use of the 5/4 cut-point measure for binge drinking is a valuable tool for understanding and preventing college drinking problems.

the 5/4 threshold measure of heavy episodal drinking is a valuable tool to identify students who experience alcohol-related harms, but it should be used in conjunction with other tools to identify students at risk for more severe alcohol problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selection of an alcohol cut-point should be based on the purpose for which the measure is being used.

the 5/4 cut point for binge drinking is useful for identifying college students at risk for experiencing harms and is a useful screening tool for identifying students who may need further clinical evaluation and intervention.

a 5/0 or a 5/1 drink cut-point may be more useful in identifying students who are experiencing negative consequences of alcohol use and who may be at risk for alcohol-related problems than higher drink thresholds.
